event: Nala tells Wat no one is hunting her, but she is owned by no village either.
She says that may make the village unsafe for her, and asks if there is any other way to heal.
She asks whether more levels, or better stats, would be enough to mend her.
Wat grunts at "hunting", as if a stone has been set down that he was carrying.
He answers the level question first, and flatly: a level makes you harder, not whole.
He says a hurt still wants rest and care, whatever the letters say; a leveled man bleeds the same.
Rest heals, he says: sleep under a roof, eat, and keep off that foot, and a body mends itself.
He says the temple at Wenmarch heals with light, for silver, and that is two days on past the ford.
Neither of them, he says, has silver to spare for a stranger's foot, and he says it without shame.
Jory comes back in for the kettle, and Wat tells him what she said about the village.
Jory thinks about it with the kettle in his hand; then he says he is a Brackenford man.
He says his mother is headwoman there, and one he speaks for goes through the gate unasked.
Wat says guest-right is a night and a breakfast; after that it is work, pay or the road.
He slaps his knee and says his knees are bad for sitting the clamp at night.
Someone has to sit up with it and call out if it flares, and he would sooner sleep.
He says a guest who sits the night watch eats at this fire till the raft goes down.
Jory says that in five days she would ride the raft to Brackenford with them, spoken for.
Wat looks at her across the fire and asks whether she can sit awake in the dark and not panic.
